questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Initial Consonant Sound /w/ with Vowel Letter
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct article:
"The beggar was carrying ___ one-rupee note in his tattered pouch."
questions.explanation: Word 'one' written vowel letter 'O' se shuru hota hai, lekin iska spoken phonetic sound /wʌn/ ('wa' - Hindi vyanjan sound) hai. English phonetics ke rule ke mutabiq initial consonantal sound /w/ ke pehle indefinite article 'A' lagta hai. Isliye 'a one-rupee note' correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Words opening with /w/ take 'A'.
questions.hint: 'One' bolte waqt opening sound 'wa' nikalta hai jo consonant sound hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the appropriate article for the sentence:
"The hearing was adjourned for ___ hour to allow the counsel to examine the new witness."
questions.explanation: Word 'hour' mein initial letter 'h' silent hota hai aur word ka spoken sound /aʊər/ ('aa' vowel sound) se shuru hota hai. Vocalic opening sound hone ke karan indefinite article 'AN' lagega: 'an hour'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Silent 'h' words take 'AN'.
questions.hint: 'Hour' mein 'h' silent hai aur aawaz vowel sound se shuru hoti hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct option:
"The candidate holds ___ B.Tech degree in Computer Science and an LLB degree in Law."
questions.explanation: Initialism 'B.Tech' ko pronounce karte waqt pehla letter 'B' bola jata hai, jiska sound /biː/ (consonant sound 'ba') hai. Consonant sound se shuru hone ke karan indefinite article 'A' lagega: 'a B.Tech degree'. Dusri taraf 'LLB' /el/ vowel sound se shuru hota hai isliye wahan 'an LLB' laga hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Consonant initialisms take 'A'.
questions.hint: Letter 'B' bolte waqt consonant sound 'ba' nikalta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the correct combination of articles:
"A clerk misplaced ___ file on Friday. After an extensive search, ___ file was recovered from the records room."
questions.explanation: Pehle sentence mein 'file' first time introduce ho rahi hai (any random singular countable file), isliye indefinite article 'a' lagega. Doosre sentence mein 'file' wahi particular file hai jo Friday ko ghum hui thi (second mention / identified entity), isliye definite article 'the' lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Definite Article 'The' — First mention takes 'a/an'; subsequent mention takes 'the'.
questions.hint: Pehli baar unknown cheez introduce hoti hai ('a'), dobara aane par specific ban jati hai ('the').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct articles:
"___ moon shines by reflecting light from ___ sun."
questions.explanation: Jo entities hamare universe ya solar system mein unique (apne aap mein ek hi) hain, unke naam ke aage standardly definite article 'The' lagta hai. Isliye 'the moon' aur 'the sun' dono ke pehle 'The' lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Definite Article 'The' — Unique natural entities take 'The'.
questions.hint: Sun aur Moon nature mein unique hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the correct articles for the blanks:
"This is ___ most comprehensive commentary on the Constitution, and it covers ___ first ten amendments in detail."
questions.explanation: Superlative degree adjective ('most comprehensive') ke aage hamesha definite article 'The' lagta hai ('the most comprehensive'). Ordinal numbers ('first', 'second', 'tenth') jo sequence batate hain, unke aage bhi 'The' lagta hai ('the first ten amendments'). Isliye dono blanks mein 'the' aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Superlatives & Ordinals — Both superlative adjectives and ordinal numbers mandate 'The'.
questions.hint: Superlative ('most') aur ordinal ('first') dono 'The' demand karte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blanks:
"The sacred river ___ Ganges flows across northern India, whereas ___ Lake Pichola is situated in Udaipur."
questions.explanation: Rivers (nadiyon) ke naam ke aage conventional rules ke mutabiq definite article 'The' lagta hai ('the Ganges', 'the Yamuna'). Lekin single individual lakes (jheelon) ke naam ke aage standard English mein article KABHI NAHI lagta ('Lake Pichola', 'Lake Superior'). Isliye pehle mein 'the' aur doosre mein Zero Article (no article) aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Conventional Geography — Rivers take 'The'; Individual lakes take Zero Article.
questions.hint: Rivers ke aage 'The' lagta hai, par individual lakes ke aage article nahi lagta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Country Names: Political Terms vs Ordinary Names
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct articles:
"The trade delegation flew from ___ United Kingdom to ___ India to attend the summit."
questions.explanation: Country ke naam mein agar 'Kingdom', 'States', 'Republic', ya plural word shamil ho, toh definite article 'The' lagta hai ('the United Kingdom', 'the USA', 'the Netherlands'). Lekin ordinary geographical countries ke naam ke aage Zero Article lagta hai ('India', 'France', 'Japan'). Isliye 'the United Kingdom' aur 'India' (no article) correct pair hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Conventional Geography — Countries with 'Kingdom/States/Republic' take 'The'; single sovereign names take Zero Article.
questions.hint: 'Kingdom' political descriptor hai jo 'The' leta hai; 'India' sovereign name hai jo article nahi leta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the correct articles for the blanks:
"He has been learning ___ French for two years, and he admires ___ French for their rich culinary culture."
questions.explanation: Pehle blank mein 'French' language (bhasha) hai, aur languages ke naam ke sath zero article lagta hai ('learning French'). Doosre blank mein 'French' France ke logon (nationality / people as a whole) ko represent kar raha hai, isliye wahan definite article 'The' lagega ('the French' = the French people).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Zero Article Omission — Language = Zero Article; Collective Inhabitants = 'The'.
questions.hint: Language ke aage article nahi lagta, par country ke logon ke group ke aage 'The' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Institutional Purpose: Primary vs Secondary Location
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blanks:
"The key witness was summoned to ___ court to testify, while the IT technician came to ___ court to install new display monitors."
questions.explanation: Witness court mein gawahi dene (judicial justice / primary functional purpose) ke liye gaya hai, isliye Zero Article ('summoned to court'). IT technician wahan kisi litigation ke liye nahi, balki equipment repair/install karne (incidental visit / secondary purpose) gaya hai, isliye 'the court' aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Institutional Expressions — Primary functional role takes Zero Article; Secondary physical visit takes 'The'.
questions.hint: Gawahi dena court ka primary kaam hai, monitor lagana secondary visit hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct words:
"The legal brief was printed on high-grade ___ (A) / and the senior counsel published ___ (B) on administrative jurisprudence."
questions.explanation: Word 'paper' dual-usage noun hai. Jab 'paper' printing material ya substance ki tarah use ho, toh ye UNCOUNTABLE hota hai aur bina article ke aata hai ('printed on paper'). Jab iska matlab scholarly essay, research article, ya newspaper ho, toh ye COUNTABLE ban jata hai aur 'a paper' leta hai ('published a paper'). Isliye (A) paper, (B) a paper correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06 & Study Guide Sec 6: Dual-Usage Noun Countability.
questions.hint: Material substance uncountable hota hai, par scholarly essay countable hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Uncountable Noun Quantification with Unit Counters
questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: The retired judge gave me an advice regarding the administrative exam.
The retired judge gave me a piece of advice regarding the administrative exam.
The retired judge gave me many advices regarding the administrative exam.
The retired judge gave me two advices regarding the administrative exam.

questions.explanation: 'Advice' uncountable noun hai jiske aage direct 'an' lagana (*an advice) ya plural '-s' lagana (*advices) strict error hai. Uncountable noun ko singular discrete unit mein express karne ke liye partitive unit counter 'a piece of advice' use kiya jata hai. Isliye Option (B) completely correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & PIT-02: Uncountable Noun Article Intrusion & Unit Counters.
questions.hint: 'Advice' uncountable hai, isliye 'a piece of advice' bola jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Few vs A Few in Positive Encouraging Context
questions.question:
Select the correct quantifier for the blank:
"Don't panic about the approaching deadline; we still have ___ days left to file the rejoinder."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka context encouraging aur reassuring hai ('Don't panic', 'we still have... left'). Positive availability (kuch din bache hain) express karne ke liye plural countable noun 'days' ke sath quantifier 'A FEW' aayega. 'Few' negative scarcity batata jo 'Don't panic' se bilkul match nahi karta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Countable Quantifiers — 'A few' denotes positive existence ('some') with plural countable nouns.
questions.hint: 'Don't panic' kehkar tasalli di ja rahi hai ki waqt bacha hai, isliye positive quantifier 'a few' aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: The Few with Defined Plural Group
questions.question:
Choose the correct determiner:
"___ few advocates who were present in the bar room signed the condolence resolution."
questions.explanation: Noun phrase 'few advocates' ke sath qualifying relative clause 'who were present in the bar room' aayi hai. advocates ki sankhya kam thi, lekin wo sabhi jo wahan present the un sabhi ne sign kiya (all of that small group). Is specific aur comprehensive reference ke liye 'The few' aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Countable Quantifiers — 'The few' denotes all of that small identified number.
questions.hint: Relative clause 'who were present' specific group ko define kar rahi hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Little vs A Little in Scarcity Context
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate quantifier:
"The prosecution had ___ evidence to substantiate the conspiracy charge, resulting in the acquittal of the accused."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka outcome 'acquittal of the accused' (bari ho jana) hai. Case tabhi gira kyunki saboot na ke barabar (almost zero) tha. Uncountable noun 'evidence' ke sath negative deficiency aur scarcity express karne ke liye quantifier 'LITTLE' aayega. 'A little' saboot ki maujoodgi batata jo acquittal se contradict karta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Uncountable Quantifiers — 'Little' denotes negative insufficiency ('almost none').
questions.hint: Accused bari ho gaya kyunki saboot na ke barabar tha (negative context).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the correct option for the blank:
"The flood destroyed ___ little grain that the farmer had stored for the harsh winter months."
questions.explanation: Noun 'grain' uncountable hai aur uske sath clause 'that the farmer had stored' aayi hai. Farmer ke paas anaj kam hi tha, par wo sara ka sara jo usne store kiya tha flood mein destroy ho gaya (all of that small amount). Is exhaustive specific meaning ke liye 'The little' use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Uncountable Quantifiers — 'The little' denotes the whole of that small specified quantity.
questions.hint: 'That the farmer had stored' bache huye poore anaj ko specify kar raha hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Non-Assertive Any in Negative and Conditional Contexts
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate determiner:
"The magistrate passed the injunction without ___ hesitation, having perused the urgent petition."
questions.explanation: Preposition 'without' inherently negative meaning rakhta hai (bina kisi). Negative aur non-assertive contexts mein standard determiner 'ANY' use hota hai: 'without any hesitation'. 'Some' affirmative expressions mein aata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Some vs Any — Negative triggers (without, hardly, scarcely, not) demand 'ANY'.
questions.hint: 'Without' negative word hai jiske sath 'any' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence:
"Many a prospective candidate ___ failed to clear the preliminary examination due to poor time management."
questions.explanation: Construction 'Many a + Singular Countable Noun' hamesha SINGULAR VERB leta hai. Meaning 'many candidates' (plural) ke barabar hota hai, lekin syntax distributive hone ki wajah se singular auxiliary 'has' aayegi: 'Many a prospective candidate has failed'. Options (A), (C), aur (D) plural verbs hain jo concord violate karti hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Study Guide Sec 10: 'Many a + Singular Noun + Singular Verb' Concord Formula.
questions.hint: 'Many a' ke baad singular noun aur singular verb ('has') aati hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Either/Neither for Two vs Any/None for Three or More
questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: Neither of the five writ petitions was entertained by the court.
None of the five writ petitions was entertained by the court.
Either of the five writ petitions was entertained by the court.
Neither of the five writ petitions were entertained by the court.

questions.explanation: 'Neither' aur 'Either' strictly DO (2) entities ke liye use hote hain. Yahan total paanch (5) petitions hain, isliye negative ke liye 'None' use hoga. Sath hi 'None of the five petitions' formal English mein singular verb 'was entertained' leta hai. Isliye Option (B) completely error-free hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & PIT-06: Distributive Entity Limits — Use 'None' for 3 or more entities.
questions.hint: Paanch (5) petitions hain, isliye 'Neither' nahi, 'None' aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
In the following sentence, find the part containing a grammatical error:
"The registry provided (A) / a valuable information (B) / regarding the revised roster (C) / of the Division Bench. (D)"
questions.explanation: Part (B) mein error hai. 'Information' uncountable noun hai, iske pehle indefinite article 'a' lagana (*a valuable information) strict grammatical error hai. Sahi construction ya toh 'valuable information' hogi ya 'a piece of valuable information' hogi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & PIT-02: Uncountable Noun Article Intrusion Trap.
questions.hint: 'Information' uncountable noun hai jiske aage 'a' nahi lag sakta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10
